name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q01 - Units of rate constant for reaction orders

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Reaction Order)List II (SI Units of Rate Constant)
A. Zero-order reactionI. \(\text{s}^{-1}\)
B. First-order reactionII. \(\text{mol}^{1/2}\cdot\text{L}^{-1/2}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}\)
C. Second-order reactionIII. \(\text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}\)
D. Half-order reactionIV. \(\text{mol}^{-1}\cdot\text{L}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of item A
For an \(n^{\text{th}}\)-order reaction, the general unit of the rate constant is \((\text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1})^{1-n}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}\). For a zero-order reaction (\(n = 0\)), the unit is \((\text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1})^{1-0}\cdot\text{s}^{-1} = \text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}\), matching unit III.

Step 2: Evaluation of item B
For a first-order reaction (\(n = 1\)), the unit is \((\text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1})^{1-1}\cdot\text{s}^{-1} = \text{s}^{-1}\), matching unit I.

Step 3: Evaluation of item C
For a second-order reaction (\(n = 2\)), the unit is \((\text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1})^{1-2}\cdot\text{s}^{-1} = \text{mol}^{-1}\cdot\text{L}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}\), matching unit IV.

Step 4: Evaluation of item D
For a half-order reaction (\(n = 1/2\)), the unit is \((\text{mol}\cdot\text{L}^{-1})^{1-1/2}\cdot\text{s}^{-1} = \text{mol}^{1/2}\cdot\text{L}^{-1/2}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}\), matching unit II.

Step 5: Matching Synthesis and Final Answer
Pairing each reaction order with its corresponding SI unit yields A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.
Final Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q02 - Chemical reactions and their kinetic reaction categories

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Chemical Reaction)List II (Kinetic Classification)
A. Decomposition of ammonia on hot platinum at high pressureI. First-order chemical reaction
B. Hydrogenation of etheneII. Pseudo-first-order reaction
C. Acid-catalyzed hydrolysis of ethyl acetate in excess waterIII. Nuclear first-order decay
D. Radioactive disintegration of radium-226IV. Zero-order heterogeneous catalytic reaction

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of item A
The decomposition of gaseous ammonia on a hot platinum catalyst at elevated pressure saturates the active metal surface, making the reaction rate independent of ammonia concentration. Thus, it is classified as a zero-order heterogeneous catalytic reaction (IV).

Step 2: Evaluation of item B
The hydrogenation of ethene according to \(\text{C}_2\text{H}_4(\text{g}) + \text{H}_2(\text{g}) \to \text{C}_2\text{H}_6(\text{g})\) follows the differential rate law \(\text{Rate} = k[\text{C}_2\text{H}_4]\), which represents a classic first-order chemical reaction (I).

Step 3: Evaluation of item C
In the acid hydrolysis of ethyl acetate, water is present in enormous excess so that its concentration remains virtually unchanged throughout the reaction, simplifying the second-order rate expression to a pseudo-first-order reaction (II).

Step 4: Evaluation of item D
All natural and artificial radioactive decays of unstable nuclei, including the alpha-decay of radium-226, follow first-order kinetics strictly governed by nuclear decay constants (III).

Step 5: Matching Synthesis and Final Answer
Combining these kinetic characteristics yields the one-to-one correspondence A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.
Final Answer: A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q03 - Integrated rate equations and half life formulas

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Kinetic Parameter)List II (Mathematical Expression)
A. Integrated rate equation for zero-order reactionI. \(t_{1/2} = \frac{[\text{R}]_0}{2k}\)
B. Exponential concentration expression for first-order reactionII. \([\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0 - kt\)
C. Half-life expression for zero-order reactionIII. \(t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{k}\)
D. Half-life expression for first-order reactionIV. \([\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0 e^{-kt}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of item A
Integrating the zero-order differential equation \(-\frac{\mathrm{d}[\text{R}]}{\mathrm{d}t} = k\) from \(t = 0\) to \(t\) yields \([\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0 - kt\), matching expression II.

Step 2: Evaluation of item B
Integrating the first-order differential equation \(-\frac{\mathrm{d}[\text{R}]}{\mathrm{d}t} = k[\text{R}]\) yields \(\ln\frac{[\text{R}]}{[\text{R}]_0} = -kt\), which upon exponentiation gives \([\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0 e^{-kt}\), matching expression IV.

Step 3: Evaluation of item C
Setting \([\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0/2\) in the zero-order equation gives \(kt_{1/2} = [\text{R}]_0/2\), so \(t_{1/2} = \frac{[\text{R}]_0}{2k}\), matching expression I.

Step 4: Evaluation of item D
Setting \([\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0/2\) in the first-order equation gives \(t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{k} = \frac{0.693}{k}\), matching expression III.

Step 5: Matching Synthesis and Final Answer
Matching each kinetic parameter with its mathematical formula produces A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q04 - Linear kinetic plots and their corresponding slopes

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Linear Graphical Plot)List II (Slope of the Straight Line)
A. \([\text{R}]\) versus \(t\) for a zero-order reactionI. \(\frac{k}{2.303}\)
B. \(\ln[\text{R}]\) versus \(t\) for a first-order reactionII. \(-\frac{E_a}{R}\)
C. \(\log\left(\frac{[\text{R}]_0}{[\text{R}]}\right)\) versus \(t\) for a first-order reactionIII. \(-k\) with vertical intercept \(\ln[\text{R}]_0\)
D. \(\ln k\) versus \(\frac{1}{T}\) in the Arrhenius equationIV. \(-k\) with vertical intercept \([\text{R}]_0\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of item A
For a zero-order reaction, \([\text{R}] = -kt + [\text{R}]_0\). A plot of \([\text{R}]\) versus \(t\) yields a straight line with slope \(-k\) and intercept \([\text{R}]_0\), matching item IV.

Step 2: Evaluation of item B
For a first-order reaction, \(\ln[\text{R}] = -kt + \ln[\text{R}]_0\). A plot of \(\ln[\text{R}]\) versus \(t\) yields a straight line with slope \(-k\) and intercept \(\ln[\text{R}]_0\), matching item III.

Step 3: Evaluation of item C
Rearranging the first-order rate law gives \(\log\left(\frac{[\text{R}]_0}{[\text{R}]}\right) = \left(\frac{k}{2.303}\right)t\). A plot against \(t\) passes through the origin with slope \(\frac{k}{2.303}\), matching item I.

Step 4: Evaluation of item D
The logarithmic Arrhenius equation is \(\ln k = -\left(\frac{E_a}{R}\right)\left(\frac{1}{T}\right) + \ln A\). Plotting \(\ln k\) against \(1/T\) produces a straight line with slope \(-\frac{E_a}{R}\), matching item II.

Step 5: Matching Synthesis and Final Answer
Correlating each graph with its specific linear slope gives A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.
Final Answer: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q05 - Percentage completion times for first order reactions

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Extent of First-Order Reaction)List II (Time Required in Terms of Rate Constant \(k\))
A. \(50\%\) completionI. \(\frac{2.079}{k}\)
B. \(75\%\) completionII. \(\frac{0.693}{k}\)
C. \(87.5\%\) completionIII. \(\frac{6.909}{k}\)
D. \(99.9\%\) completionIV. \(\frac{1.386}{k}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of item A
For \(50\%\) completion, remaining amount is \(0.5[\text{R}]_0\). \(t_{50\%} = \frac{2.303}{k}\log 2 = \frac{0.693}{k}\), matching II.

Step 2: Evaluation of item B
For \(75\%\) completion, remaining amount is \(0.25[\text{R}]_0 = [\text{R}]_0/4\), which corresponds to 2 successive half-lives. \(t_{75\%} = 2 \times \frac{0.693}{k} = \frac{1.386}{k}\), matching IV.

Step 3: Evaluation of item C
For \(87.5\%\) completion, remaining amount is \(0.125[\text{R}]_0 = [\text{R}]_0/8\), corresponding to 3 successive half-lives. \(t_{87.5\%} = 3 \times \frac{0.693}{k} = \frac{2.079}{k}\), matching I.

Step 4: Evaluation of item D
For \(99.9\%\) completion, remaining amount is \(0.001[\text{R}]_0 = 10^{-3}[\text{R}]_0\). \(t_{99.9\%} = \frac{2.303}{k}\log(10^3) = \frac{6.909}{k} \approx 10 t_{1/2}\), matching III.

Step 5: Matching Synthesis and Final Answer
Evaluating the logarithmic multiplier for each completion stage gives A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q06 - Mechanistic features of elementary and complex reactions

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Reaction Entity)List II (Defining Mechanistic Feature)
A. Elementary reactionI. Proceeds via a sequence of steps; overall rate controlled by the bottleneck step
B. Complex reactionII. Provides an alternate reaction pathway with reduced activation energy without being consumed
C. Reaction intermediateIII. Occurs in a single event where molecularity and reaction order are identical
D. CatalystIV. Chemical species formed during an intermediate step and consumed before final products emerge

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of item A
An elementary reaction occurs in a single isolated collision event; for all elementary reactions, the order with respect to each reactant equals its molecularity (III).

Step 2: Evaluation of item B
A complex reaction occurs through a sequence of elementary steps termed the mechanism; its overall rate is dictated by the slowest rate-determining step (I).

Step 3: Evaluation of item C
A reaction intermediate (such as \(\text{IO}^-\) in the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide) is produced in an early elementary step and completely consumed in a subsequent step, never appearing in the net balanced equation (IV).

Step 4: Evaluation of item D
A catalyst interacts chemically with reactants to form a low-energy activated complex, increasing the reaction velocity, and is regenerated chemically unchanged upon completion (II).

Step 5: Matching Synthesis and Final Answer
Assigning each kinetic entity to its defining mechanistic feature gives A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.
Final Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q07 - External parameters and their kinetic acceleration mechanisms

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Change in Condition)List II (Physical / Molecular Consequence)
A. Increase in reactant concentrationI. Broadens Maxwell-Boltzmann curve and roughly doubles fraction with \(E \ge E_a\)
B. Rise in temperature by \(10\text{ K}\)II. Increases number of accessible active adsorption sites on the surface
C. Addition of a positive catalystIII. Increases number of molecular collisions per second per unit volume
D. Finely dividing a solid catalystIV. Decreases activation energy barrier equally for forward and backward processes

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of item A
Increasing the concentration increases the number of molecules per unit volume, which directly raises the collision frequency \(Z\) (III).

Step 2: Evaluation of item B
A \(10\text{ K}\) rise in temperature shifts the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution, nearly doubling the area corresponding to molecules possessing energy \(E \ge E_a\) (I).

Step 3: Evaluation of item C
A positive catalyst provides an alternate reaction pathway with a lower potential energy barrier, reducing \(E_a\) equally for both directions (IV).

Step 4: Evaluation of item D
Finely dividing a solid catalyst drastically increases its specific surface area, providing more active catalytic sites for adsorption of reacting molecules (II).

Step 5: Matching Synthesis and Final Answer
Connecting each reaction condition alteration to its fundamental kinetic consequence yields A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.
Final Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q08 - Arrhenius parameters and collision theory kinetic factors

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Kinetic / Collision Theory Term)List II (Physical Interpretation)
A. Pre-exponential factor \(A\)I. Probability factor reflecting proper geometric molecular alignment during collision
B. Activation energy \(E_a\)II. Frequency factor representing the total collision rate per unit concentration
C. Steric factor \(P\)III. Fraction of colliding molecules possessing kinetic energy \(E \ge E_a\)
D. Exponential factor \(e^{-E_a/RT}\)IV. Energy difference between the activated complex and the reacting ground state

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of item A
The Arrhenius pre-exponential factor \(A\) is the frequency factor, directly related to the total bimolecular collision frequency \(Z_{AB}\) in the system (II).

Step 2: Evaluation of item B
Activation energy \(E_a\) is the energy required to lift reacting species from their average reactant energy level to the peak of the activated complex barrier (IV).

Step 3: Evaluation of item C
The steric factor \(P\) is introduced in collision theory (\(k = P Z_{AB} e^{-E_a/RT}\)) to account for the probability that colliding molecules possess mutually favorable spatial orientations to facilitate bond transformation (I).

Step 4: Evaluation of item D
The Boltzmann exponential factor \(e^{-E_a/RT}\) represents the fraction of total molecules in the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution having energy equal to or exceeding \(E_a\) (III).

Step 5: Matching Synthesis and Final Answer
Aligning each collision theory term with its precise physical meaning gives A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.
Final Answer: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q09 - Reaction order dependence of half life periods

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Reaction Order)List II (Half-Life Proportionality with Initial Concentration \([\text{R}]_0\))
A. Zero-order reactionI. \(t_{1/2} \propto [\text{R}]_0^0\) (independent of initial concentration)
B. First-order reactionII. \(t_{1/2} \propto [\text{R}]_0^{1-n}\) (general \(n^{\text{th}}\)-order relation)
C. Second-order reactionIII. \(t_{1/2} \propto [\text{R}]_0^1\) (directly proportional to initial concentration)
D. General \(n^{\text{th}}\)-order reaction (\(n \ne 1\))IV. \(t_{1/2} \propto [\text{R}]_0^{-1}\) (inversely proportional to initial concentration)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of item A
For a zero-order reaction, \(t_{1/2} = \frac{[\text{R}]_0}{2k}\), which means \(t_{1/2} \propto [\text{R}]_0^1\) (III).

Step 2: Evaluation of item B
For a first-order reaction, \(t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{k}\), which contains no concentration term, so \(t_{1/2} \propto [\text{R}]_0^0\) (I).

Step 3: Evaluation of item C
For a second-order reaction, integration yields \(t_{1/2} = \frac{1}{k[\text{R}]_0}\), meaning \(t_{1/2} \propto [\text{R}]_0^{-1}\) (IV).

Step 4: Evaluation of item D
For a general \(n^{\text{th}}\)-order reaction where \(n \ne 1\), dimensional analysis and integration demonstrate that \(t_{1/2} \propto [\text{R}]_0^{1-n}\) (II).

Step 5: Matching Synthesis and Final Answer
Pairing each reaction order with its initial concentration power dependence yields A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.
Final Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMICAL_KINETICS_MCQ_Q10 - Quantitative temperature dependence and activation energy calculations

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Kinetic Situation / Problem)List II (Calculated Value / Quantitative Law)
A. Reaction rate doubles for a \(10\text{ K}\) rise from \(298\text{ K}\) to \(308\text{ K}\)I. \(\log\left(\frac{k_2}{k_1}\right) = \frac{E_a}{2.303 R}\left[\frac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2}\right]\)
B. Two-temperature integrated Arrhenius relationshipII. Activation energy \(E_a \approx 52.9\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\)
C. Fraction of molecules with \(E \ge E_a\) when \(E_a = 209.5\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\) at \(581\text{ K}\)III. \(x = e^{-E_a/RT} \approx 1.47 \times 10^{-19}\)
D. Reaction rate quadruples for a \(20\text{ K}\) rise from \(293\text{ K}\) to \(313\text{ K}\)IV. Activation energy \(E_a \approx 52.9\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of item A
Using the Arrhenius formula \(\log 2 = \frac{E_a}{2.303 \times 8.314}\left[\frac{10}{298 \times 308}\right]\), solving for \(E_a\) gives \(E_a = \frac{0.3010 \times 19.147 \times 91784}{10} \approx 52.897\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1} \approx 52.9\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\) (II).

Step 2: Evaluation of item B
Subtracting \(\ln k_1 = -\frac{E_a}{RT_1} + \ln A\) from \(\ln k_2 = -\frac{E_a}{RT_2} + \ln A\) and converting to base-10 logarithm gives \(\log\left(\frac{k_2}{k_1}\right) = \frac{E_a}{2.303 R}\left[\frac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2}\right]\) (I).

Step 3: Evaluation of item C
The fraction of molecules with \(E \ge E_a\) is \(x = e^{-E_a/RT}\). Taking \(\log x = -\frac{E_a}{2.303 RT} = -\frac{209500}{2.303 \times 8.314 \times 581} = -18.832\). Taking antilog gives \(x = 10^{-18.832} = 10^{0.168 - 19} \approx 1.47 \times 10^{-19}\) (III).

Step 4: Evaluation of item D
If the rate quadruples (\(k_2/k_1 = 4\)) between \(293\text{ K}\) and \(313\text{ K}\), \(\log 4 = 0.6021 = \frac{E_a}{19.147}\left[\frac{20}{293 \times 313}\right]\). Solving gives \(E_a = \frac{0.6021 \times 19.147 \times 91709}{20} \approx 52.86\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1} \approx 52.9\text{ kJ}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\) (IV).

Step 5: Matching Synthesis and Final Answer
Matching each calculation problem with its exact numerical result or governing formula gives A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.
Final Answer: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
